title: A Warrior's Code of Prayer
subtitle: Forty Days of Prayer for Men Who Work While Others Sleep
reader: Men who work nights and weekends in uniform. Border Patrol, police, fire, medics, corrections, military, and the men who used to and are still carrying it.
reader_problem: He believes, more or less. He has not prayed a real prayer in months. The devotionals he has been handed were written for a man with a calm week and a quiet house, and they do not survive contact with a night shift.
promise: Forty short prayers built for a man standing post, written in the language he actually uses.
transformation: He goes from praying only in emergencies to holding a short, honest, daily position that survives shift work, fatigue, and a job that does not stop.

units.title: Taking the Post
units.thesis: Showing up on time is the first act of faith, and it counts even when nothing happens.

units.title: The Hours Nobody Sees
units.thesis: Work done where nobody is watching is not wasted work.

units.title: Fear on Station
units.thesis: Courage is fear that took the post anyway, and God never asked you to stop feeling it.

units.title: Tired Is Not Weak
units.thesis: Fatigue is a physical condition, not a character defect, and it needs rest rather than repentance.

units.title: The Boredom Watch
units.thesis: Most of the job is nothing happening, and how you hold the nothing decides how you handle the something.

units.title: Eyes Up
units.thesis: Vigilance is a discipline you rebuild every shift, not a trait you either have or do not.

units.title: The Radio Goes Quiet
units.thesis: Silence from above is not absence, and you already know this from every long night on a dead net.

units.title: End of Shift
units.thesis: How you close a shift decides what you carry into the house.

units.title: What You Carry
units.thesis: You are carrying more than your gear and you have never once written it down.

units.title: The Call You Remember
units.thesis: One call sits on top of the stack for every man, and it does not go away by being ignored.

units.title: Anger in the Truck
units.thesis: Anger is information about something you have not dealt with yet.

units.title: The Guilt You Kept
units.thesis: Guilt over a decision made in four seconds needs a verdict, not a rerun.

units.title: Men Who Did Not Make It
units.thesis: Grief for the ones who are gone belongs out loud, at least once, to somebody.

units.title: The Body Keeps Time
units.thesis: Your body is keeping a record of this work whether or not you agree to read it.

units.title: Drinking It Down
units.thesis: Every man in this work is offered a cheap way to stop feeling, and it always sends a bill.

units.title: Asking for Help
units.thesis: Asking for help is a tactical decision, and men who cannot make it get other people hurt.

units.title: Walking In the Door
units.thesis: The first ninety seconds inside your own house set the next twelve hours.

units.title: Your Wife Is Not the Enemy
units.thesis: Threat posture at home reads as contempt, and she is not wrong to name it.

units.title: The Kid Who Waited Up
units.thesis: Presence is measured in minutes given, not in hours intended.

units.title: Teaching a Boy to Stand
units.thesis: Your son learns what a man does by watching what you do when you are tired.

units.title: What You Say at the Table
units.thesis: What a family talks about at dinner becomes what the children believe is normal.

units.title: The Days You Miss
units.thesis: You will miss birthdays and games, and how you handle the miss matters more than the miss.

units.title: Keeping One Promise
units.thesis: One promise kept on a bad day outweighs ten made on a good one.

units.title: Rest That Is Not Collapse
units.thesis: Real rest is scheduled and protected, not what is left over after you fall down.

units.title: The New Guy
units.thesis: How you treat the newest man tells the whole crew what the standard actually is.

units.title: Leading Tired Men
units.thesis: Leadership on hour fourteen is mostly about lowering the noise and naming the next task.

units.title: The Supervisor You Hate
units.thesis: You still have to work for him, and how you do it is a decision about you.

units.title: Loyalty With a Spine
units.thesis: Loyalty that cannot say no is not loyalty, it is fear wearing a friendship.

units.title: Getting Passed Over
units.thesis: A board, a list, or a promotion is not a verdict on your worth as a man.

units.title: Keeping Your Word In Writing
units.thesis: Reports, statements, and logs are where your integrity becomes a record.

units.title: When You Were Wrong
units.thesis: A clean, fast admission costs less than every version of covering it.

units.title: The Man You Trained
units.thesis: Multiplication is the only thing you build in this job that outlives your tenure.

units.title: The Long Career
units.thesis: Twenty years is a distance event and you cannot sprint it from the front.

units.title: The Body Slows Down
units.thesis: The day you cannot do what you did at twenty-five is a planning problem, not a shame problem.

units.title: Who You Are Without the Badge
units.thesis: Identity welded to a job title comes apart on the day the job ends.

units.title: Retirement Is a Deployment
units.thesis: Leaving the work needs a plan with dates in it, the same as any other movement.

units.title: The Man at the Funeral
units.thesis: Go to the funeral. Stand where people can see you. Say the name out loud.

units.title: What Gets Written Down
units.thesis: The doctrine you write outlives you, and most men never write any of it.

units.title: Handing Off the Post
units.thesis: A relief briefing is an act of care, and so is everything else you hand the next man.

units.title: Standing Down
units.thesis: You will put this work down one day, and the man who put it down well started practicing early.
